newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Holiday torpor lulls market.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Holiday torpor lulls market.

text.p: The traditional August torpor is beginning to cast a spell over Asian debt markets, as holidays take a toll of new issue activity.
"It's official -- everyone's on holiday," said one, commenting on the dearth of issuance, apart from some recent Asian yankees in the United States.
Also contributing to the slowdown is the currency softness in Asian markets, with the spillover effect making pricing new offshore issues difficult, bankers said.
Among the few new deals expected, Kookmin Bank is expected to pay "in the mid-40s" for its US$100 million floating rate note (FRN) issue, bankers said
The three year FRN will also feature annual puts and calls, they said.
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi and ABN Amro have submitted proposals for the deal but no mandate has been awarded.
Kookmin on Thursday announced net interim profits were up just over 12 percent.
In other news, the South Korean government is planning to funnel US$300 million to merchant banks, funnelling it out of US$1 billion in emergency loans from the Bank of Korea.
The Bank of Korea said this week that it had supplied US$1 billion to seven commercial banks which were suffering U.S. dollar shortages.

In other news, Broadsino Investment Co Ltd, a unit of Jiangsu International Trust and Investment Corporation (JITIC), has mandated Natexis Banque-BFCE to arrange a US$30 million secured three year FRN.
General syndication is expected towards the end of the month, when the market and volumes are up, bankers said.
JITIC is the largest provincial trust and investment corporation in China.
In the Philippines, the peso was weak again after a four-percentage point cut in the overnight rate to 14 percent.
The Philippines interbank offered rate fell early on Thursday after the overnight rate cut.
In India, Tata Electric Companies said its first international issue, a US$300 million bond attracted "strong investor demand" in New York earlier this week.
It said it attracted more than US$600 million in bids, although the two-tranche deal was not increased.
